data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'kristos' meaning pure, clear or anointed. In Christianity, the name Krysta is associated with the Messiah or anointed one. The name Krysta carries the meaning “Pure, Clear” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Krysta usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, clear and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Krysta belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, Clear.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Krysta total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: קריסטה
in_hebrew.meaning: אבן נוצרייה שמשמעותה עוקבת אחר המשיח
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קריסטה הוא נגזר מהמילה היוונית κρυστός (khristos) שמשמעותה המשיח, ופירושו עוקבת אחר המשיח. השם הוא סמלי לנוצרים ומבטא את הקשר הרוחני שלהם עם ישוע המשיח. השימוש בשם זה נפוץ בקרב נוצרים שונים ברחבי העולם.

in_greek.name: Κρυστα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κρυστα προέρχεται από το ελληνικό χρυστός (khristos), που σημαίνει ο Θεός ή ο Αντίχριστος, και συγκεκριμένα αναφέρεται στη σχέση με τον Ιησού Χριστό. Στην παράδοση των πρώτων Χριστιανών, το όνομα αυτό ήταν έντονα συνδεδεμένο με την πίστη και την αφοσίωση στον Χριστό.

historical_references.reference: The legend of Saint Cristina the Martyr, born in the 3rd century AD in Sirmium, modern-day Croatia, tells the story of a young virgin who was executed for her refusal to sacrifice to Roman gods. The name 'Cristina' is a derivative of 'Christian' and was a common name for Christian martyrs during this period.

Another reference to the name 'Krysta' can be found in the 15th century AD in the Czech Republic, where a statue of the Virgin Mary was named 'Panna Krystova' or Our Lady of Charity of Kruševce. This statue is said to have miraculous healing properties and is a popular pilgrimage site for Christians in the region.
